clue.text: Tooth job, one out for you, say

indicators.note: one thing goes out and another comes in for it, so a letter of the job word is swapped

parts.note: a job is a task
A is one, as in 'a' single thing
the letter U sounds like the word 'you'

explanation.surface: A dentist's job: pulling a tooth, with one more done for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of TASK is swapped out and U put in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's or walrus's long protruding front tooth is called this, so it is a kind of tooth.

clue.text: Deal endlessly with Germany over zilch? It's doomed to failure

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word deal is dropped

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket

explanation.surface: A trade deal with Germany coming to nothing is a hopeless venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal endlessly' drops the last letter to give DEA. 'Over' just places D above DUCK in the down entry. A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a plan or project with no chance of success is called this, as useless as a shot bird.

clue.text: I'm taken aback by fashion — it's an illusion

indicators.note: taken back, so the letters of I'm are read in reverse order

parts.note: the letters of I'm without the apostrophe
a rage is a craze or fashion, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a fashion trend decides it's all an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert that is not there.

clue.text: Was unfaithful to Elizabeth to begin with at Derby race

indicators.note: to race is to rush about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order
only the starting letter of the name Elizabeth is used

explanation.surface: Someone cheated on Elizabeth at the Derby, the famous English horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like the Derby itself but signals mixing E (Elizabeth's first letter) with the letters of AT DERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to betray a partner is to be disloyal or unfaithful to them.

clue.text: Fellow left foreign exchange discount

indicators.note: the fellow has left, so his letter departs
the letters of the word foreign exchange places with one another

explanation.surface: A man walked out of the foreign exchange desk without his discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign exchange' reads as currency trading; actually the letters of FOREIGN are rearranged once the F (Fellow) has 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to discount a claim is to disregard it or pay it no attention.

clue.text: 750 grammes resting on new oven?

parts.note: three quarters of a kilo, so three of the four letters of KILO

explanation.surface: A recipe: put 750 grammes of something on top of a new oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 750 grammes is three quarters of a kilo, so the first three of its four letters. In a down entry 'resting on' puts KIL above N.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a furnace for firing pottery or drying, a kind of oven, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Idle miners come first regarding 1984?

indicators.note: the miners' piece is placed ahead of the comedian's in the answer

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union
Eric Idle is a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.surface: Striking miners took precedence in the news during 1984.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 1984-85 British miners' strike, and Eric Blair (George Orwell) wrote the novel 1984. 'Idle' is the surname of Python Eric Idle.
explanation.definitionFit: 1984 is a number, so anything concerning it is to do with numbers, the adjective's sense.

clue.text: 'Bird training's no good!', you shout at home

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise training

indicators.note: a shout is said aloud, so the word is heard as a sound, a letter

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, sounds like the letter U
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A frustrated owner yells at home that teaching their pet bird is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A penguin is a flightless seabird of the southern hemisphere, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Children go back to front on slide

indicators.note: the back letter of the word for children moves round to the front

parts.note: kids are children

explanation.surface: Children are lining up at the back to go on the playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a car or foot skids when it slides out of control on a slippery surface.

clue.text: A loud bird gets egg on time

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a tern is a seabird
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A noisy bird is encouraged to lay an egg on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' looks like 'encourage', but egg gives O and on stands as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between noon and evening is a time of day.

clue.text: Worth mentioning old Labour leader's upset over special summit

indicators.note: the reversed name is split and goes over, around, the other letters
in a down entry, upset turns the leader's name upside down, reading it from bottom up

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
a summit is a peak

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader is upset about a special summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' means the reversed name is split to go around the other letters; Michael Foot led the British Labour Party in the early 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom, usually after a negative, as in 'no money worth mentioning', meaning of any significance.

clue.text: Building hospital by a river

parts.note: H is the map and signage abbreviation for hospital
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in Sussex

explanation.surface: A building is described as the hospital beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a house is a building for people to live in.

clue.text: Cat steals last of Stilton from paradise

indicators.note: the letter is stolen, taken away from the word for paradise

parts.note: heaven is paradise

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word Stilton is used

explanation.surface: A cat sneaks off with the end of a Stilton cheese, a little paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat is not the animal: in slang to cat is to vomit. Stilton is an English blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to cat means to be sick, and to heave also means to retch or vomit.

clue.text: Small boys go crazy over shelled peas and vegetables

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go over, around, the inner letters
the letters of the word boys go wild into a new order
shelled peas lose their pods, so each word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Little boys are going wild about their plates of shelled peas and vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go crazy' rearranges BOYS to OYBS, which goes 'over' EA and N, the shelled middles of PEAS and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans, from an Asian legume, are eaten as a vegetable, so they are examples.

clue.text: Perhaps Lancelot ousts king in the dark

indicators.note: the king is thrown out of the word, so his letter is removed

parts.note: Sir Lancelot is a knight of the Round Table, one example
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Lancelot overthrows King Arthur under cover of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness between sunset and sunrise are the time referred to, a synonym.

clue.text: Coat's a hit with detached hood

indicators.note: the hood is the head, so the top letter is taken off

parts.note: a smack is a hit

explanation.surface: A coat is described as a hit, with a removable hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' is the covering at the top, so the word loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for mackintosh, a British word for a waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Pretentious person dupes drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of dupes lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A pretentious person tricks drunks.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal noun for someone who pretends to intellectual knowledge, a poser.

clue.text: Soundly in favour of young people as they build muscle

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the word for young people is heard by ear, said aloud

parts.note: teens are young people, teenagers

explanation.surface: Someone firmly supports youngsters as they bulk up in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary nutrients made of amino acids are what the body uses to grow and repair muscle.

clue.text: Club wants women to gain advantage

indicators.note: wants means lacks, so the club word is missing the letter

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club wants more women members to get ahead of rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: having the edge over someone means having an advantage over them.

clue.text: Reagan's campaign slogan's a little bit negative!

parts.note: elect is the call of an election slogan: vote for this candidate
Ronald Reagan, US President, went by Ron

explanation.surface: Reagan's campaign slogan is a bit of negative campaigning!
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a tiny subatomic particle carrying a negative charge, a little bit of negativity.

clue.text: Externally, bishop wearing stole produces a bible

indicators.note: the stole is worn around the inner letters, so they go inside

parts.note: stole means took, the past of steal
EXT is the abbreviation for external or externally
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop wears his stole and produces a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a bishop's vestment but is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a bible is an authoritative reference book on a subject, the standard one.

clue.text: Dances with Nato abstainers?

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet T is Tango, so TT, teetotal, abstainers become Tango Tango

explanation.surface: Dancers join up with the countries that stayed out of NATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballroom dances of Argentine origin; and a whimsical name for teetotallers, TT people, in NATO alphabet speak.

clue.text: Speedy ships

definitions.meaning: fast, swift, as in ... of foot
a navy's group of ships sailing together

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective meaning swift, and a noun for a group of naval vessels.

clue.text: Halt! After small change to starter, I'm stuffed

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word for halt is changed

parts.note: to pull up is to halt, stop a vehicle
f. is the short form of following, so after, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Stop! After a small change to my starter, I can't eat another bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course but means the first letter: P of PULL UP becomes F.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you are full up means you have eaten enough, an informal way of saying you are stuffed.

clue.text: Great flow under construction

indicators.note: construction is building something new, so the letters of flow under are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A great flow of traffic is going past the construction site.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something wonderful is great, marvellous.

clue.text: Comedian to court daughter

parts.note: to woo is to court romantically
D is the genealogy abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A comedian tries to court a man's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria Wood was a much-loved British stand-up comic and comedy writer.

clue.text: Cultivated part of flower, trimming both sides

indicators.note: both ends are cut off, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a stamen is the pollen-bearing part of a flower

explanation.surface: A gardener trims both sides of a flower in a cultivated bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tame plant is one grown in gardens rather than wild, so cultivated, domesticated.

clue.text: Extra serious weather problem ends terribly for planet

indicators.note: terribly suggests things going wrong, so those letters are scrambled
only the final letters of each of these four words are used

explanation.surface: A dreadful weather problem ends badly for the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends' takes A, S, R and M; 'terribly' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, an example of a planet.

clue.text: Oblong — a shape for a sausage?

indicators.note: to shape is to mould into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Is an oblong a good shape for a sausage?
explanation.definitionFit: A large smoked sausage named after the Italian city, also called baloney or mortadella.

clue.text: Drink bitter from start to finish? Just stories

parts.note: rum is a drink

indicators.note: the starting letter of the bitter word moves to the finish

parts.note: sour means bitter

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a bitter all evening, just telling tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumours are unverified tales passed around, nothing more than stories.
